issues.what: The stops share nearly identical timing and camera grammar: centered globe, straight scale-up, terrain, edge exit, then bare stars. The individual terrain angles vary, but the stop-to-stop rhythm becomes predictable.
issues.fix: Change the cadence and approach geometry at two stops: let Jupiter lead with an off-axis moon-to-storm track and let Saturn enter along the ring plane without repeating the centered push.

issues.what: The last hold is almost unchanged, with Neptune cropped against the left edge and the distant point too small to become a clear second focal point. The lookback reads more like a parked exit than a final reframe.
issues.fix: Let the pullback settle on a deliberate planet-to-distant-light composition: give Neptune more left-edge clearance and ease a small reframe toward the distant point before locking off.

issues.what: Mars slips abruptly up and out, several samples contain only stars, then Jupiter goes from a pinprick to a large near-centered globe over very few samples. The final closing move is compressed relative to the transit pause.
issues.fix: Start the Jupiter reveal earlier or carry an identifiable target through the gap, and spread the final growth over more frames so the approach eases naturally into the hold.

issues.what: The orbit view pushes toward a broad canyon strip, but the landing introduces a new horizon and a foreground ridge without a clear screen-space landmark carried across.
issues.fix: Aim the last orbital frames at one canyon bend and keep it at a consistent screen position as the camera pitches down into the terrain approach.

issues.what: The opening has a strong silhouette, but the loop and sunspot remain nearly centered throughout, so the full terrain beat changes little before the scale reset.
issues.fix: Keep the initial read, then add a short lateral creep so the near sunspot shifts relative to the loop and the opening has a distinct camera beat before the pullback.
